how: Calls seek several forms of Magic representation rather than one continuously agreed build.
Builders describe divided attention, difficult solo work and designs outmatched by occupied space.
Recruiting unfamiliar readers includes explaining pixel placement and the event before they can join.
A template receives a brief commitment to stay and help make the card back.
Acceptance can require instructions, while a separate refusal gives no reason, limiting any universal bare-acceptance and reasoned-refusal rule.
A proposer, template maker and volunteer distribute starting work across members rather than establishing a permanent leader.
Members propose alternative emblems and negotiate additions without thereby adopting every proposal collectively.
Members report joining an existing border and share the location where their work has begun.
Reference images, grid layouts and anchor coordinates turn proposals into instructions for placing.
Posting a guide does not settle unresolved background colors or establish that its scale fits the chosen site.
Members report a running script and discuss a bot whose contribution is later described as limited.
Machine use alone cannot establish upkeep pressure as its cause or successful automation when the participant reports little benefit.
A proposed strawpoll establishes neither enacted decided order nor the truth of an aggregate frequency claim.
Participants promise protection after completion and request coordinates to monitor their corner.
A completion report directly receives a promise to protect the finished work.
Upkeep must distinguish authorized edits from vandalism, prompting advance coordination so defenders do not undo legitimate alterations.
Anticipating mistaken repairs does not demonstrate an investigation attributing actual changed pixels.
Participants seek acceptable space and permission from neighboring territories before securing a viable mark.
Diplomacy can seek entry and prospective protection before upkeep of an established mark, so maintenance is not its sole local precursor.
The candidate hosting process appears as requests for permission and protection, without establishing that a host accepted the proposed arrangement.
Urging contact with neighbors does not identify an envoy actually carrying an authorized proposal between rooms.
An outsider appeals against destroying maintained art, while an internal reply rejects a raid for its anticipated cost.
Appeals by threatened outsiders must remain distinct from demonstrated restraint or compliance by the target-building room.
One member reports defending another community's mark, while reciprocal defense for a host remains proposed.
A suggestion to team with Italy after an overrun does not show formation of an alliance.
Builders report restarting after takeover and later abandoning Chandra for another plan.
Loss and insufficient hands can end in quitting after a restart rather than compel another relocation.
Disagreement with subreddit moderation does not establish disagreement over authority to bind placers to an interroom treaty.
Proposed diplomacy without an observed treaty or compliance dispute cannot establish the tentative agreement-to-authority-dispute mechanism.
The candidate identity condition appears in existing Magic lore, emblem proposals and fandom role-play rather than a newly constituted nation.
A sports fan's appreciation does not show a preexisting quarrel being carried into the Magic campaign.
Recalled opponents are not a preexisting tie named in the same turn as a call to attack.
Members stage fake previews and products, acknowledge being fooled and extend fictional product rules.
April Fools licence is contested where spoiler-season trust and prank avoidance conflict with preserving surprise.
Participants authenticate purported previews through physical card conventions, image details and collector numbers rather than merely play along.
Participants judge comic effort, repetition and timeliness separately from whether the fabricated image is technically convincing.
Theme membership alone cannot make late fake-spoiler posts into recruitment when their concepts concern jokes rather than canvas action.
Members dispute removals and moderation priorities while a megathread provides a venue and others route organizing elsewhere.
Repeated calls precede boundary drawing, but conflicting removal accounts do not establish a flood-based motive for every deletion.
Participants explicitly describe deletions as obstructing coordination and answer that obstacle by offering a dedicated organizing thread.
Members announce completion, thank contributors and credit additions to the reported card-back corner.
Achievement must remain target-specific because celebration of the completed corner coexists with failed Chandra work.
Participants recall failed work and dispute later impressions of whether the final card survived.
Post-close replies correct accounts of nonparticipation and destruction by asserting that a sticky and surviving card-back image showed the room's contribution.
Correcting textual accounts does not establish independent image verification or participation in a cleaned-copy project.
A successor-canvas proposal elicits a tool recommendation and a reported first pixel, while another request receives refusal.
Successor building follows a direct venue recommendation, while recollection of the old image occupies another branch and is not established as its cause.
A recommendation of successor-canvas affordances directly receives acceptance, coordinates and a report of one pixel placed.
The prohibition on placing after original closure must be canvas-specific because later successor-canvas placing is explicitly reported.
Members propose converting existing art, destroying an allegedly unclaimed blob and considering a raid without demonstrating those attacks occurred.
A proposed destructive conversion receives a warning to obtain territorial permission or risk being wiped.
A proposed raid receives a refusal explicitly justified by its expected fatal cost to the builders.
A participant retrospectively names groups fought over Chandra without establishing mutual taunts or a victory campaign.
